headline: President Obama created an emergency board to look into a labor dispute between Philadelphia-area commuter rail operator SEPTA and its train engineers.
what_it_does: This order sets up an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) and its locomotive engineers, who are represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen union. Emergency boards like this are used under federal railroad labor law to study a dispute and report on it. While that process runs, both sides generally must hold off on strikes or lockouts. The title does not give the details of the dispute or the board's findings.

who_it_affects.how: Their union's dispute with SEPTA goes to a federal board for review, which generally delays any strike while the board does its work.
The agency's dispute with its engineers is reviewed by a federal board, and it generally cannot change working conditions or lock workers out during that time.

who_it_affects.group: Commuter rail riders in the Philadelphia region
who_it_affects.how: Their train service is less likely to be interrupted by a strike while the board reviews the dispute.

when_it_takes_effect: October 10, 2014, when the order was signed
